title: A new heaven and a new earth (Revelation 21:1–4)
word: A new heaven and a new earth
hookLine: God will dwell with them; no more death, mourning, crying or pain

cards: Which way does heaven move? One familiar picture points up: when it's all over, people go up there. Revelation twenty-one points the other way.
John sees the new Jerusalem, and it isn't waiting above the clouds for anyone to climb to.
It's coming down: "And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband."
After the beasts, the fallen city and the thousand years, the closing vision of the Bible isn't people leaving earth. It's heaven arriving.

teach.h: A NEW HEAVEN, AND NO MORE SEA.
teach.b: First, the opening line: "And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea."
Isaiah had heard God promise it: "For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth." John sees it happen. And no more sea.
In chapter thirteen, the beast rose from the sea. Some readers hear its absence as the end of chaos and danger; others as the end of distance, nothing left to divide people.

teach.h: GOD PITCHES HIS TENT WITH US.
teach.b: Second, God moves in: "Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God."
Tabernacle is the old word for a tent, like the one Israel carried through the desert for God's presence. At the end, God pitches the tent among people.

Third, what's gone: "And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away."
Not new things added; old things missing. No funerals. No hospitals.
No crying in the car before you go inside. Fourth, now. Christians who read it this way say it isn't only a picture of later.
It's the shape they hope toward, and some say it's why they visit the sick and sit with the grieving today: practicing a world where God lives next door.

how: Revelation 21:1–4 is read at Christian funerals and memorial services, and Christians speak of it as the hope behind visiting the sick, comforting the grieving and caring for the earth.

games.q: what does “a new heaven and a new earth” mean?
o: creation renewed, with God dwelling among his people
a second planet where the saved are taken after death
the sky and land remade after Noah's flood

games.q: a new heaven and a new earth — tap the pairs.
p: coming down from God out of heaven
the end of chaos, or of distance

s: in Revelation 21 the faithful leave earth and go up to the city
the city comes down from God out of heaven.
Isaiah heard a promise of new heavens and a new earth
"for, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth."
Revelation 21:4 lists new things added to the world
it lists what's missing: death, sorrow, crying and pain.

games.q: John sees the holy city, new Jerusalem. which way is it moving?
o: up, carrying the faithful away from earth.
down, coming from God out of heaven.
nowhere; it stays hidden behind the clouds.
games.why: it comes down, "prepared as a bride adorned for her husband," and a voice says God will dwell with people. the end of the story is heaven arriving.

practice: Picture one place where people cry, a hospital waiting room, a courthouse hallway, a kitchen after bad news, and let it slowly change: the chairs empty, no one waiting for a call, no one hiding red eyes.

Stay with that for a few breaths; if you pray, say Revelation twenty-one, verse four, slowly, and if not, let the picture rest. Then ask what one small thing would make that room a little more like it.

wordCard.voice: A new heaven and a new earth. John's vision in Revelation twenty-one: the old order passed away, God dwelling with people, and death and crying gone.

orig.note: Greek: a tent, a dwelling. the word the King James renders tabernacle in Revelation 21:3.

carryVoice: Your line: no more tears. Not people leaving earth, but the holy city coming down. See you tomorrow.
